recipes.name: Candied Citrus Peel
ingredients_raw: 1 cup orange peel, cut into strips

steps.text: Place peel strips in large saucepan and cover with water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes longer. Drain. Repeat this process two more times.

In a medium saucepan, heat sugar and 1/4 cup water over high heat until boiling. Place peel in sugar mixture, reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes, until sugar is dissolved. Remove peel with slotted spoon and dry on wire rack overnight. Store in airtight container.

raw_recipe.headline: Candied Citrus Peel
raw_recipe.description: With this easy 2-step process, you can make candied orange peel -- or any other citrus peel -- with little mess and fuss.

video.description: With the help of a few leftover orange peels, you’ll be enjoying a crispy and sugary snack! In this video, Natalie shows you how to make candied citrus peels using either orange, grapefruit, lemon, or lime peels. Boiled multiple times over the stove, these crisp fruit candies can be enjoyed with minimal ingredients and little cleanup.

review.reviewBody: Super! so happy to find a basic recipe for candied citrus peel! Added notes: For gorgeous presentation, cut citrus peel in spiral. For result more citrus peel-y and less candy-fied... do step 1 only 2x (instead of 3x), also skip the 10 min simmer.
This was easy. After they dried I tossed them in granulated sugar. A tip to make the removal of the pith super easy - use a Pampered Chef grapefruit knife. You'll be done in a jiffy.

Tastes just like gumdrops...only better! Easy to do, but beware it takes some time, mostly "babysitting". Worth it though! Dipped them in sugar while still a little sticky and will use them to decorate a lemon bundt cake. Thanks for the great recipe!

I used just-overripe Cuties, with the concession that if the peel has considerably less pith and the fruit is squishier toss it. A 5 lb bag makes a pint of juice and 4-5 cups of peels.The result is that any remaining tannins make your tongue tingle without tasting bitter.The prep was easy enough for my 3 year old to help. But next time it'll be even easier because they can just be quartered. With such a thin peel they're prone to breaking after boiling and if you think the strip is too big you're as wrong as I was. I put some clingwrap on the counter under the rack for easy and quick cleanup.After 8 hours I tossed some more sugar in a small container and the 1/2 of the peels in small batches. The peels were more sticky than tacky. The sugar clung to the sticky and not much else.After 8 more hours, I repeated the sugar coating process on 1/2 of the remaining peels and the sugar only clung to the pith and the parts of the peels that were on the rack - grill marks, bud. The rest i tossed in the convection oven for 40 min at 170º F (the lowest setting) checking every 20 minutes, the peels weren't tacky after 40 minutes and the sugar coating process was done while warm and it was by far the most uniform. Next time I'll quarter them and dry for 16 hours and bake-dehydrate then warm-coat.

This was easy but took a little time. I'm delighted with the result. It's well worth doing this to have around for recipes where you might ordinarily use expensive store products loaded with preservatives. I'll definitely do it again. Definitely double it, which takes about 2 large oranges.

I've wanted to try this for a long time and finally, yesterday, I did it. Yes, I did have to babysit the boiling water & peels through a few rounds, but I had other things to do in the kitchen, so no bother. After the rounds of boiling, I rolled the orange scraps in sugar and set them in a dehydrator for a bit. W.O.W. They taste like that gummy orange slice candy you can find at the store, but with more citrus zing! I love this- this will definitely be a regular treat in our house.

I made this with lemon and orange (miniola) peel. I boiled the lemon 4 times. They came out picture perfect. I boiled the Orange three times. They began to turn mushy, so I stopped there. The flavor is wonderful. Not bitter. I left the pith on. Some recipes have you remove it. This is pretty labor and time intensive as it is. I will probably do multiple batches around the holidays for stollen and fruit cake. The husband loves the syrup for tea. So much better than store bought.

As posted, this recipe fails to mention removal of the pith before boiling. I scrape off as much of the pith as possible without ruining the peel. May I also suggest saving the left-over sugar water for your coffee or tea. Delish!
Great recipe. I used mandarin oranges and added Italian lemon juice and Blood Orange gummies to Medicate them. Delicious!!!

I have found Candied Lime Peel very difficult to make--it often turns out like strips of linoleum--too hard and tough to use even minced. The secret is to STOP boiling the strips in the sugar syrup BEFORE all the pith becomes transparent. You want some white still showing.

Excellent! My first time making candied orange peel and it was a huge success. I love this! As someone else remarked, tasted almost like those orange jelly candies. Orange flavor just erupts in your mouth! I used a veggie peeler to peel the orange so it wasn't beautiful (I was using the peel in a recipe) so no pith. A little time is spent but the flavor is big. Will definitely make this again and again. Thank you!

It was an amazing recipe; I had never known there was something this easy that only needed 3 ingredients! The only thing is didn't quite like is the burns, I burned myself too hard, being as clumsy as I am, lol, blisters aren't a new thing. The flavors were really nice, at one point being nicely sweetened and the other being bitter slightly, it was bittersweet! Altogether great candy!
Used the recipe as is, except in the end I mixed sugar with a bit of citric acid and sodium bircarbonate and then mixed the peels to coat and to give it a sour/sherbet taste
Fantastic recipe. Everyone that has tried the Candied Mandarin Peel absolutely loved it. Great candy. 👍🍋🍊
It was fun to make, but they are bitter. I'll be able to use them in Christmas breads. Not sure what went wrong.
These keep for a long time and retain a wonderful citrus flavor. I use a combination of lemon, grapefruit, and orange skin.
Always use my orange peel with this recipe. Love surprising my friends with this treat, they love it 😊

As someone else pointed out, REMOVE THE PITH FIRST because I didn't know that, then saw the comment, and had to scrape down hot peels. It was annoying and time consuming, lol.... my bad. But I've never made this before. Maybe it's easier this way, unsure. The simple syrup is great! I had leftovers, as I calculated before removing the pitch, so have saved it as a syrup. It's pale orange and tastes wonderful. Anyway REMOVE THE PITH. Peels turned out great. I don't have a wire rack so put it on a tray on tinfoil, very easy to do. Thanks! But update the recipe re pith. Cheers and happy holidays!
i also used these candies cut up to put on top of sugar cookies for decoration. they look like stain glass and add flavor.
